message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I am p4 with $125 cash and two Get Out of Jail Free cards. I own a yellow monopoly with one house on each property, plus several unmortgaged orange and red properties. The opponent is p3.

The opponent has $1627 and owns a full dark blue monopoly, all four railroads, and several hotels. I have no mortgaged properties and no Get Out of Jail Free cards. I just paid $1100 rent on Pacific Avenue and mortgaged Park Place. I am deciding whether to end my turn or propose a trade with p3.

Selling the yellow houses would yield about $225. Mortgaging MEDITERRANEAN or NEW_YORK would add roughly $130. The opponent's light blue hotels, pink four-houses, and green four-houses are all major threats.

I am calculating the exact board positions to determine how far p3 must roll from Boardwalk to reach my yellow properties.

I mapped the full board. From Boardwalk, the opponent's next roll cannot land on any of my properties. The farthest they can reach is St. Charles with a 12, which belongs to them.

The opponent cannot land on my yellows for at least two rolls. They would need 27 spaces to reach them, while their nearest unmortgaged properties are only 16 to 20 spaces away.

The opponent is not an immediate threat from their movement. The real danger is my next roll from Pacific Avenue.

Rolling 2 lands on North Carolina with four houses, which would cost about $1050. Rolling 4 lands on Pennsylvania Avenue with four houses, another large rent. Rolling 5 hits the Short Line railroad for $200. Rolling 7 or 9 lands on mortgaged properties where I collect no rent. Rolling 10 hits GO for $200. Rolling 11 lands on Mediterranean, which is mine.

I am calculating the exact rent values for these green properties.

Standard Monopoly rent values are now confirmed. Rolling 2 on North Carolina costs $1100, and rolling 4 on Pennsylvania Avenue costs $1200. With only $125 cash, even mortgaging Mediterranean and New York for about $130, plus selling the three yellow houses for $225, yields roughly $480 total. That is still short of the required amount, so landing on either of those properties would bankrupt me.

Rolling 5 on Short Line costs $200, which I can cover with mortgaged properties and cash. Rolling 8 on Luxury Tax costs $100, which I can also pay. The only rolls that guarantee bankruptcy are 2 and 4, totaling four of thirty-six possible outcomes. Unmortgaging properties costs money rather than generating cash.

I am now considering whether to propose a trade with p3. They own all the properties that would bankrupt me, so they might be willing to trade them away for something in return.

The opponent has no incentive to trade. They are winning decisively and want me to land on the green properties and bankrupt. I have the only yellow monopoly, which they could use to complete a new set. I also own all three orange properties, though two are mortgaged. They do not need my dark blue properties since they already hold Boardwalk.

Trading away the yellow monopoly would eliminate my only income source and give the opponent another deadly set. They already own Baltic, so Mediterranean would complete a weak brown monopoly. I cannot trade for a green property to break their four-house green monopoly because they will never exchange it for anything I have. My net worth is far too small to threaten one green rent.

A rejected trade proposal would still consume my turn, so I must only offer deals that are actually worth accepting. I am now considering whether to ask for Illinois from the opponent.

I realized that trading for Illinois would not help. I already own Kentucky and Indiana, but both are mortgaged. Unmortgaging them would cost about $121 each plus interest, and I have no cash for building. A red monopoly is not an immediate survival tool.

I do not need to mortgage now. The engine lets me liquidate during the debt resolution phase after I roll, so I can wait until I actually owe money rather than locking in cash beforehand.

Pre-emptive mortgaging would not save me from the upcoming rolls, and it would reduce future income. New York Avenue and Mediterranean Avenue generate almost no rent while mortgaged, so keeping them unmortgaged offers little benefit. I also cannot build any houses right now because I have no cash for construction.

Unmortgaging the two orange properties would cost about $99 each, leaving me with no spare cash. Even with a full orange monopoly, the rent would only be roughly $32 per turn, which is not enough to survive the upcoming rolls.

Selling the yellow houses would cut my income from $110 to $44 per turn. I will keep them and end my turn.

I will pass this turn. I have no urgent need for jail cards, and the yellow monopoly is my only viable income source. The opponent is on Boardwalk and cannot reach my properties, so they pose no immediate threat. My turn will follow theirs, and I must survive the upcoming roll from Pacific Avenue.

A roll of 6 on the Chance space could land me on Illinois for $20, or on the nearest railroad for $200. Other cards like "pay poor tax" are manageable.

The opponent can reach Mediterranean Avenue in one roll from Boardwalk. I will mortgage it now so they collect no rent.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

I'm p4 in a 1v1 against p3. I just paid $4 rent to them and have $321 cash. I own 10 properties total: MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE, NEW_YORK_AVENUE, and three others are mortgaged. I also have one house on each of ATLANTIC_AVENUE, VENTNOR_AVENUE, and MARVIN_GARDENS.

I calculated the probability of each roll. Eleven of thirty-six rolls are safe. Three are cheap. Thirteen are deadly.

Rolls 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10 cost $550 to $900. I can cover the first two with full liquidation. The last four are instant death.

Rolls 2 and 11 land on railroads for $200. That is manageable.

Liquidating before the roll cannot save me from unaffordable rent. The engine only allows mortgaging and selling when I actually owe money. Pre-liquidating is pointless for survival.

I am now considering building more houses on my yellow properties. Each house costs $150. I have one house on each yellow street. I must build evenly.

I cannot afford to build three houses on my yellow properties. Even one house would cost $150 and leave me with only $171 cash.

The rent from two houses on any single yellow street is still well below p3's $931. Building more houses on my yellows will not threaten them enough to matter.

I cannot afford to build three houses on my yellows. That would cost $900, and even two houses would cost $450.

Selling my houses would give me cash but destroy my only weapon, and rebuilding would be difficult.

Unmortgaging both St. James and Tennessee would leave only $23 after building one house, so the orange rent would still be too low to threaten p3.

Trading is also unwise. If I gave p3 the red properties, they would complete a red monopoly with hotels costing over $1,000 each. If I traded Mediterranean Avenue for Baltic, they would own the brown monopoly.

Neither player currently owns a brown monopoly, so trading Mediterranean Avenue would not give p3 a free brown hotel. They would likely demand something valuable in return, such as a railroad or Illinois Avenue, but that exchange is unappealing because I have no railroads and Illinois alone pays only $20 in rent.

I have two get-out-of-jail-free cards. I will keep them as a safety net and avoid building, unmortgaging, or trading to preserve cash for survivable rolls.

Three are safe rolls, and three are railroads costing two hundred dollars.

I am now considering a desperate trade proposal. I would offer p3 my entire yellow monopoly, orange properties, dark blue holdings, Mediterranean Avenue, utilities, both get-out-of-jail-free cards, and all remaining cash in exchange for something valuable.

I realized that breaking p3's green monopoly would force them to sell their hotels back to the bank. That would instantly wipe out their biggest income source and turn the game around. I am now weighing whether I can trick them into trading a green property for my entire empire.

Trading a property from a monopoly with buildings requires selling the hotels first, so the engine might reject the offer. Even then, p3 would not accept a green hotel for my entire portfolio because it would not threaten them. I also realized that unmortgaging my red properties would complete a red monopoly.

Unmortgaging both Kentucky and Indiana would cost $242, leaving only $79. I cannot complete a red monopoly because p3 already owns Illinois. Trading for Illinois would give them the red set while I receive just $20 in rent. I am now considering offering cash for that property.

I realized that if I go bankrupt to p3, they inherit all my properties automatically. They have no incentive to trade me anything useful now. I will simply end my turn.

I considered mortgaging Mediterranean Avenue and New York to raise cash, but realized the engine only allows mortgaging when I actually owe money, so doing it now would be pointless. I also calculated the exact cash shortfall for a $550 hit. I would need to mortgage Mediterranean Avenue and New York, then sell both houses to survive. That leaves me with only one house and almost no cash.

Pre-building would reduce my available cash even more, so I will not build or sell houses.

message.reasoning:
The user needs to pay $550 in rent with a $199 shortfall. They have mortgaged properties and sellable buildings available.

Mortgaging New York Avenue yields $100, leaving a $99 shortfall. Selling houses on Atlantic, Ventnor, or Marvin Gardens returns $75 each. Only one action can be taken at a time.

Opponent p3 has hotels on nearly all properties and four railroads. The rent of $550 comes from the hotel on Vermont Avenue.

Selling all three yellow houses would raise $225, covering the shortfall and leaving $26 cash. Mortgaging New York Avenue first would only bring cash to $451, still leaving a $99 gap that requires selling houses anyway. The strategy prioritizes preserving yellow houses as the main defensive weapon, but paying this rent is mandatory or bankruptcy follows.

The prior thought assumed mortgaging Mediterranean Avenue for $30 would clear the $550 rent. That mortgage was already applied, yet cash remains at $351 and the shortfall is still $199. The prior estimate was wrong.

Standard rent for one house on each yellow property is only $110 to $130. That is too small to threaten an opponent with $931 cash and a $550 rent payment coming from this turn.

Selling all three houses would reduce their rent to roughly $44–$52, making them even weaker. The better path is to sell the houses now for $225 and leave New York unmortgaged, ending with $26 cash while preserving the property. Mortgaging New York first would still require selling at least two houses afterward to cover the remaining $99 shortfall.

Mortgaging New York Avenue first would still leave a $99 shortfall. Selling two yellow houses afterward would raise $150, leaving $51 cash and one house on one property. This is viable because Monopoly allows uneven house distribution by one.

The opponent is currently in Jail at space 10. The board layout from Jail is being mapped to assess the next roll.

The board map from Jail is complete. A roll of 1 lands on St. Charles, 2 on Electric Company, 3 on States, 4 on Virginia, 5 on Penn RR, 6 on St. James, and 7 on a Community Chest.

Rolling 8 lands on Tennessee, which is mortgaged and collects no rent. Roll 9 lands on New York Avenue, but it still only pays base rent of $16 because the other two orange properties are mortgaged and break the monopoly bonus. Roll 10 lands on Free Parking, and roll 11 lands on Kentucky, which is also mortgaged.

The opponent cannot reach the yellow properties this turn. The maximum roll from Jail is 12, which lands on Indiana Avenue, a mortgaged property that collects no rent. Yellow houses are completely useless as a defensive weapon for the next turn. After paying the $550 rent, the player will remain on Vermont Avenue.

The opponent will roll from Jail next, then the player, then the opponent again. Yellow houses could matter on p3's second roll after they move. Cash after payment will be minimal, but bankruptcy is not required because enough cash can still be raised.

The player holds two jail cards, which would allow them to avoid a turn in Jail if they are sent there. The total liquidation of $325 is sufficient to cover the $199 shortfall. New York Avenue is not worth mortgaging because unmortgaging it later would cost an extra $10.

Selling all three houses now leaves the player with $26 cash and no houses, but New York Avenue stays unmortgaged. Mortgaging New York first and selling two houses afterward would leave one house and roughly $51 cash, though New York would be mortgaged. Liquidating all three houses is the better choice because rebuilding them later would require $150 each, which is impossible with only $26 remaining.

Keeping one house is the better strategy. Rebuilding from zero costs $450 total, so preserving a single house saves $150 and maintains a meaningful rent threat. Ventnor Avenue offers the highest single-house rent at $130, but the player cannot choose which property to keep in the first action if they mortgage New York Avenue first; selling houses must happen afterward.

The player will mortgage New York Avenue first to preserve the yellow houses as a weapon. After paying the rent, they will have almost no cash left, so building or trading on their next turn from Vermont is impossible.

Bankruptcy is rejected because the opponent would claim all properties. Even one house on each yellow property only yields $110 to $130 in rent, which is harmless against an opponent with $1481 cash. Three houses would have raised only about $800 to $900 total, still insufficient to threaten them.

The yellow houses are no longer a meaningful threat. The opponent now owns hotels on three monopolies and has $931 cash, so one house on each yellow property cannot bankrupt them.

The focus is shifting to surviving future rent payments. From Vermont Avenue, the next roll could land on St. Charles Avenue, which carries a $750 hotel rent. Electric Company is mortgaged and collects nothing.

From Vermont Avenue, the player faces four dangerous rolls. St. Charles hotel rent is $750. States hotel rent is $750. Virginia hotel rent is $900. The Pennsylvania Railroad charges $200. These four outcomes occur in eight of thirty-six possible rolls.

Liquidating all three yellow houses and mortgaging New York Avenue yields only $325 in extra cash. Combined with the current $351, total liquidity becomes $676. After paying the $550 rent, $126 remains. That is insufficient to cover the $200 railroad rent. The yellow properties can be mortgaged afterward, but only after their houses are sold.

The player is now questioning whether Monopoly rules permit mortgaging a property that still has one house while another property in the same color group has zero houses. If that rule blocks it, mortgaging New York Avenue first would leave them unable to mortgage any yellow properties afterward.

Mortgaging any property in a color group requires selling all houses on that group first. Keeping one house on a yellow property therefore blocks mortgaging any yellow property until that last house is sold. The $400 mortgage reserve for the yellows is effectively locked behind selling the final house. The player is now comparing Option A, which is to sell all three houses immediately.

Both liquidation paths yield the same total future liquidity of $526. Option A leaves the player with $26 cash and no houses. Option B leaves $51 cash, one house preserved, and New York Avenue mortgaged. The choice is therefore between immediate cash and a small rent threat.

Selling houses returns half their value, and mortgaging New York Avenue now costs the same as later. The engine allows sequential liquidation, so the only downside of keeping one house is an extra step if a yellow property must be mortgaged immediately.

Mortgaging New York Avenue now leaves $451 cash and a $99 shortfall. The next step is to sell the last yellow house for $75 and mortgage a yellow property for at least $130 to cover the remaining debt.

The engine guarantees sequential liquidation, so mortgaging New York Avenue first is safe. Ventnor Avenue will be kept as the single house because it yields the highest one-house rent at $130. Atlantic and Marvin will be sold next to raise cash.

The player will mortgage New York Avenue to cover the rent. Only that property is available for mortgage; the other options are already mortgaged or sellable buildings. This decision reverses an earlier private thought that recommended leaving New York unmortgaged.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I'm ready to play Monopoly.

I'm p4 with $51 and no properties in play. I have two get-out-of-jail cards. The opponent is p3. I'm analyzing my options.

I just paid $550 rent on Vermont Avenue. I can unmortgage Mediterranean Avenue for $33, leaving $18. I'm also considering trading with p3 or selling a house at Marvin Gardens.

Unmortgaging Mediterranean Avenue is too expensive. Selling the house at Marvin Gardens would leave me with no buildings and no threat. I'm in a terrible position against p3, who has hotels on the pink and green sets.

I'm calculating the rent potential of my yellow monopoly. Atlantic Avenue would cost $110 with one house, and Ventnor Avenue would cost $120. This is a serious threat if p3 lands there.

Marvin Gardens would cost $120 with one house. p3 has $1481 cash, so a $120 hit is trivial for them.

I cannot build houses. I have no cash for the $150 cost, and my yellow properties are unevenly developed.

Trading is also risky. Offered Park Place and Boardwalk, p3 would gain a dark blue monopoly that would be even more lethal.

I should not trade away yellows, oranges, reds, utilities, or jail cards. Each would arm p3 with a dangerous monopoly. I will focus on breaking their monopolies instead.

I cannot trade for cash without strengthening p3. Selling a property would complete a monopoly and increase their rent income.

I am calculating my next roll from Vermont Avenue. A roll of 2 lands me in jail, which is safe. A roll of 3 lands on St. Charles Avenue with a hotel.

Rolls 4, 8, and 10 are safe. Roll 7 hits the Pennsylvania Railroad for $200. I cannot pay that without liquidating assets. I can sell the house at Marvin Gardens for $75. I cannot mortgage Atlantic Avenue because no space keys are listed as mortgageable.

I cannot mortgage any yellow property while Marvin Gardens has a house. I must sell that house first.

Only Mediterranean Avenue is unmortgageable. The others cost too much to unmortgage.

I will end my turn. Selling the house at Marvin Gardens now would waste my only leverage. I will not trade away any monopolies.

Trading mortgaged dark blues for cash would backfire. p3 could unmortgage them and build hotels, making their Boardwalk hotel worth $2000 in rent. I would still be dead money. Their existing hotels already cost $550 to $1400 per visit.

Green and pink hotels are impossible to survive. Light blue was only barely manageable. The only path to victory is p3 going bankrupt. They have $1481 and can sell hotels for half their purchase price, which equals five houses. That liquidation value is enormous.

I cannot build houses. I need $150 to place one on a yellow property, but I only have $51. I am now looking for ways to raise cash without giving p3 a monopoly. Passing GO would give me $200, though many dangerous spaces lie between my current position and that square.

I now see that giving p3 one red property would not complete a monopoly, but giving both would. I own the brown set and would need to give up Mediterranean Avenue to complete it. The utilities are mortgaged and worth little rent, so trading them for cash might be viable if the price is high enough.

Trading utilities for cash would not help. Eight houses on the yellows would cost $1200, and I have only $51. One house each would cost $300. I cannot build enough to threaten p3.

I am now questioning whether any path to victory exists. I will keep my yellows, preserve my jail cards, and avoid trading sets.

- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

Mortgaging any of the three available properties will clear the $74 shortfall. I'll choose one to cover the debt.

I'm comparing the three yellow properties to decide which mortgage is best. I'm weighing rent values and future value to determine which one to mortgage now.

Marvin Gardens has the highest base rent at $24, followed by Ventnor Avenue at $22. The difference is small. I'll mortgage one of these properties to cover the shortfall.

Mortgaging Marvin Gardens would leave $66 cash after paying the rent, compared to $56 from the other two. I'll mortgage Marvin to keep the highest rent-generating property unmortgaged.

I reconsidered the mortgage choice. The $10 extra cash from mortgaging Marvin Gardens is too small to justify the $4 higher rent it would generate. I'll mortgage one of the other two yellows instead.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $56 and am on Pennsylvania Railroad. I have two jail cards. Nearly all properties are mortgaged. Only Ventnor Avenue and Marvin Gardens remain unmortgaged.

The opponent has $1,681 and owns almost all properties with hotels. I paid $200 rent on Pennsylvania Railroad.

Only Mediterranean Avenue can be unmortgaged. It costs $33, which I can afford. The other properties cost more than I have. Unmortgaging it would yield only $2 rent.

Unmortgaging Mediterranean is too expensive for the $2 rent. I will keep it mortgaged.

Mortgaging Ventnor or Marvin would give cash but destroy my only rent threats. Ventnor base rent is $22 and Marvin Gardens $24. With a full yellow monopoly they would pay $44 and $48.

Mortgaging Ventnor or Marvin would yield $130 and $140, but I would have no income properties left. The opponent has hotels on light blue, pink, and green. I am in a desperate position with only $56 cash and two jail cards. Next turn I will roll from Pennsylvania Railroad.

Rolling a 10 from Pennsylvania Railroad lands on B&O Railroad. That costs $200, which I cannot pay with only $56.

I can cover the $200 B&O Railroad rent by mortgaging Ventnor and Marvin for $270 total. Most other rolls from this space are safe. I will not pre-liquidate properties.

Trading away my dark blue or orange monopolies would be suicide. The opponent already owns hotels on light blue, pink, and green. They do not need dark blues to build hotels. I will not trade sets.

The opponent has no incentive to trade. They already own hotels and cash, so they do not need my jail cards or monopolies. Completing a brown monopoly would only yield minor rent. No trade can help me win.

Unmortgaging the dark blue properties is impossible. Park Place costs $192.50 to unmortgage and Boardwalk costs $220. I cannot afford either. The opponent's hotels are too strong for me to survive by chance alone.

I will end the turn. The $56 covers the $20 rent on Illinois. Mortgaging Ventnor and Marvin now would eliminate their rent threats before I need the cash, so I will not do it.

Mortgaging Ventnor and Marvin now would give me $270, leaving $126 after the B&O Railroad rent. I could then unmortgage Mediterranean for $33 and possibly other properties. The orange monopoly would pay $28 to $32 per turn if fully unmortgaged.

Unmortgaging all three orange properties costs $308. With $326 cash, I would have $18 left and gain a $28 to $32 orange monopoly rent. That is more than the yellow base rent of $22 to $24. The opponent is currently on St. James Place. Rent is paid when landing, not while sitting. They will roll off this space next turn.

The opponent's next roll from St. James Place could land on Ventnor or Marvin, but the resulting rent is only $22 or $24. Unmortgaging the orange monopoly would yield a single $32 hit, which is too small to offset the loss of yellow income and the $18 cash shortfall.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly.

I am player p4 with $56 cash and two Get Out of Jail Free cards. I am on Pennsylvania Railroad and have a yellow monopoly with Ventnor Avenue and Marvin Gardens unmortgaged. Most other properties are mortgaged. Player p3 has massive hotel monopolies and $1,681 in cash.

I paid $200 rent on Pennsylvania Railroad. I can only unmortgage Mediterranean Avenue with my current cash. The other mortgaged properties cost too much to unmortgage.

Unmortgaging Mediterranean Avenue is too expensive. I cannot afford to unmortgage St James either. I will not trade with p3 because they hold all winning hotel monopolies.

I own all three yellows but only Ventnor and Marvin are unmortgaged. The red monopoly is split between us: I hold Kentucky and Indiana while p3 holds Illinois.

I cannot afford to buy Illinois from p3. They would never give it up.

If they acquire my mortgaged dark blues, they could build a hotel on Boardwalk and collect $2,000 in rent. That would be catastrophic for me.

They might also want my yellows or oranges.

Mediterranean Avenue would complete their brown monopoly. A hotel there would cost $250 per turn.

I am analyzing the board from Pennsylvania Railroad. A roll of one would land me on North Carolina Avenue, a green hotel that would cost roughly $1,275 in rent. A roll of three would land me on Pennsylvania Avenue, another green hotel. The Short Line railroad is another possible destination.

Standard hotel rent values are now clear. Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut hotels cost $550 to $600 each. St Charles, States, and Virginia hotels cost $750 to $900 each. Pacific, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania hotels cost $1,275 to $1,400 each. Player p3 is currently at St James Place.

I cannot build on the yellow monopoly because Atlantic Avenue is mortgaged. I considered mortgaging Ventnor or Marvin to raise cash, but that would destroy my only rent threat and I do not need extra funds right now. Luxury tax, income tax, and railroad rent are all higher than my current balance.

I am reconsidering whether any trade could help. Player p3 might pay for a dark blue, yellow, or orange monopoly in exchange for cash or a property break.

I realized that if I go bankrupt, player p3 inherits all my assets. This makes any trade with them pointless, since they would simply win everything anyway.

I cannot threaten bankruptcy to force a trade. I cannot sell properties back to the bank. Mortgaging everything before going bankrupt would still transfer those mortgaged assets to player p3.

Mortgaging properties before bankruptcy would still leave player p3 as the winner. I considered proposing a trade that would give them yellows, oranges, or dark blues in exchange for green hotels to reduce my death risk and generate income. They would reject such an offer because it would hurt them.

I will end the turn. An empty trade was already rejected, and I have no other legal optional actions.

Player p3 can roll 8 or 11 to reach Ventnor or Marvin from St James Place. The base rent is only $22 and $24, which is negligible against their $1,681 cash. Keeping those properties unmortgaged offers no meaningful income.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to mortgage a property or declare bankruptcy.

Mortgaging Marvin Gardens would only yield $140. That leaves a $1,105 shortfall. I cannot pay the $1,275 rent even with all assets mortgaged.

There is nothing left to mortgage or sell. I will declare bankruptcy.

I am weighing whether to mortgage Marvin Gardens before declaring bankruptcy. Under standard rules, the creditor receives all assets regardless of mortgage status, but mortgaging first would give me $140 cash that p3 would receive as well.

Mortgaging first would give p3 a mortgaged property that cannot generate rent. Declaring bankruptcy now would let them claim the full-value property immediately. Either way, I cannot win.

I am on North Carolina Avenue, which p3 owns with a hotel. I have no get-out-of-jail cards that can cover the rent.

Mortgaging first would cost p3 $14 in immediate interest on the $140 cash I extract from the bank. They would still receive that money, but they would not have a clear property to collect rent from immediately. Declaring bankruptcy now gives them $30 cash plus a fully usable asset.

Mortgaging first would give p3 roughly $126 more cash than declaring bankruptcy now, but they would receive a mortgaged property instead of an unmortgaged one.

A clear property is strictly better than a mortgaged one. The recipient would pay $14 in interest to accept the mortgage, then another $154 to unmortgage it, netting no gain over receiving the clear asset immediately.
